issues.title: [Bug]: decimal division drops the IEEE 754 preferred exponent (100d/1d !== 100d, 1.00d/1d prints 1)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: 100d/1d prints 1E+2 and `q === a` is false; 1.00d/1d prints 1. Spec §6.29: 'For the decimal type, the operators differ in whether they consider the precision of the value... 1.0 == 1.00 is true but 1.0 === 1.00 is false', so precision is part of the value, and §6.20 defines decimal `/` per IEEE 754-2008, whose exact-quotient preferred exponent is Q(x)-Q(y). Clean-context check also judged `q === a` being false a spec violation (it doubted the precision requirement, but the current spec text quoted above confirms it). Root cause is decimal/decimal.go Quo(), which calls Reduce() on exact results (and normalizeUpperExponent), stripping trailing zeros; the same code is used by constant folding. Runtime arithmetic -> backend. No duplicate found (#364 is a closed, unrelated division-panic issue).

issues.title: [Bug]: invalid \u{...} escapes (surrogates, > 0x10FFFF) in string literals are accepted
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: the program compiles with no diagnostic; surrogate/out-of-range escapes become U+FFFD and the oversized escape is kept as literal text. Spec lexical grammar requires the NumericEscape CodePoint to be 0 <= n < 0xD800 or 0xDFFF < n <= 0x10FFFF, and strings exclude surrogates. Clean-context check agreed all three literals must be compile errors. Missing lexer/parser diagnostic -> frontend (a diagnostic issue, not a crash). No duplicate found.

issues.title: [Bug]: foreach over a range expression does not check the binding type (byte variable holds 257)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: compiles cleanly, and the byte/int:Signed8 loop variables hold 256, 257, 128 and 129. Spec §6.26: a range-expr's result belongs to Iterable<int,()>; §7.22.1: the typed binding pattern is used unconditionally and the compiler must check that the static types guarantee the match. int is not a subtype of byte, so this must be a compile error. The equivalent check already exists for lists (semantic_analyzer.go:2363 'invalid variable type'), but it is skipped for range expressions. Missing semantic error -> frontend. Related but not a duplicate: #1169 (range overflow at int max).

issues.title: [Bug]: non-distinct error type name is printed for `error E(...)` (prints `error E ("x")`)
issues.reasoning: Reproduces on main: `error E("x")` with a non-distinct `type E error;` prints `error E ("x")`, while `E e = error("x")` prints `error("x")`. Spec: only `distinct` induces type-ids; an error-type-reference sets the contextual type and induces E's type-ids (none here); §5.9.5 ToString names only type-ids. Clean-context check agreed both lines must print error("x"). Cause: birgen/bir_gen.go:1670-1674 puts ErrorTypeRef.TypeName into the NewError BIR instruction for any type reference, not only for distinct types, so the generated BIR is wrong -> frontend (it could also be fixed in the runtime, values/error.go writeTypeName). Not a duplicate of #1354 (that one is about missing type names in conversion errors and typedesc printing).
